patterns.name: Activity permission
patterns.question: Does the entry status permit the planned activity, or is another route needed?
fields: per activity: status, route, detail, next, checked
rules: Easy entry is not permission to work.
Each activity carries its own checked date. Never redate all activities after checking one.
New activities are added to this list; every place then shows them as unknown until vetted.
Skipped for the home country (Australia): an Australian passport holder needs no entry permission there.

patterns.name: Safety advice level
patterns.question: What level of advice does the Australian Government currently give?
rules: Advice is information for the traveller, never an automatic exclusion.
Children inherit the parent's level unless Smartraveller publishes a regional level.

patterns.name: Affection and relationships
patterns.question: How do law and custom here treat love and closeness: affection in public, couples in private (sharing a room, unmarried and same-sex couples), how marriages and partnerships are recognised, and how all of this is changing?
sources: the level's own legislation and official visitor guidance
Smartraveller's local laws, local customs and LGBTQIA+ sections
the community's own published guidance for custom
fields: items[]: area, kind (law, custom or figure), evidence when it differs from the record, text, source, checked
rules: Every item says whether it is law or custom. Custom comes from the place's own published guidance, or is labelled a signal.
Written for every visitor, whoever they love: the same question for any couple.

Changing means dated changes in law or published official figures, never impressions. UN World Marriage Data gives the average age at first marriage over time; a same-sex marriage year from a non-government list is labelled a signal.
Describe, don't moralise. No ranking of places or cultures.
Never store anything about the traveller's own relationships.

patterns.name: Ancient sites and mysteries
patterns.question: Which sites of ancient history are here (lost civilisations, mysterious temples and megaliths, underground cities, submerged ruins and sunken cities), and how can a visitor reach them lawfully: opening, tickets, permits, guides, closures, photography, diving, and the heritage laws and penalties that protect them?
sources: UNESCO World Heritage Centre (whc.unesco.org) and the UNESCO 2001 Convention states parties list
national heritage or antiquities ministries and their site pages
park and site authorities (for example Heritage Malta, English Heritage, Angkor Enterprise, Parco Archeologico dei Campi Flegrei)
fields: sites[]: name, place (place id), kind, era, what, access {opening, tickets, permits, guide, closures, photography}, protection {law, penalties}, underwater {diving, guide_or_permit, law, unesco_2001, penalties} (underwater sites only), lore {text, source (url or null), label}, sources[], checked
rules: Facts (name, era, what it is, access, protection, diving) come only from official sources: UNESCO, national heritage or antiquities authorities, park or site authorities and official tourism boards.

The lore field holds popular legends and theories (ancient aliens, lost civilisations, portals or stargates, subterranean networks, Atlantis) as claims, never facts. Start with 'Popular theories claim' or 'Local legend says'. If an official page mentions the legend, cite it in lore.source; otherwise set lore.label to 'popular lore, not an official source' and keep it brief and neutral.
Unchecked access details say 'not yet checked'. Never infer opening hours, prices or diving permission.

Underwater sites: record whether recreational diving is allowed, any licensed guide or permit, the national underwater cultural heritage law and whether the country is a party to the UNESCO 2001 Convention.

Stack layout: the country record holds national heritage law and sites; region or site records hold access rules that differ there. Note the Smartraveller advice level where it is Reconsider or Do not travel.

Themes link popular legends to real visitable places. A theme line is lore, never fact; tag sites with theme ids. A documented science fact attached to a theme (for example geomagnetic reversals from USGS) stays in its own fact field with its source.
Ancient temples are included only when ancient or legendary with notable mystery or lore attached (for example Kailasa, Borobudur, Konark). Modern working temples are not added for completeness.

themes.name: Shambhala
themes.lore: Lore: a hidden Buddhist kingdom of the Kalachakra tradition, said by popular theories to lie somewhere in the Himalaya or Central Asia.

themes.name: Shangri-La
themes.lore: Lore: a fictional hidden valley from James Hilton's 1933 novel Lost Horizon, now claimed by several Himalayan places.

themes.name: Norse myth
themes.lore: Lore: gods, giants and the world tree of the Norse sagas, linked in popular tradition to royal mounds and temple sites in Scandinavia.

themes.name: Greek myth
themes.lore: Lore: oracles, labyrinths and gods of Greek myth, such as the Delphic oracle and the Minotaur's labyrinth at Knossos.

themes.name: Sumerian
themes.lore: Lore: popular theories claim Sumerian texts describe visitors from another planet (the Anunnaki); scholars read them as myth.

themes.name: Mt Shasta
themes.lore: Lore: popular theories claim a hidden city (Telos) of survivors from Lemuria lies inside the mountain.

themes.name: Mt Hayes (Alaska)
themes.lore: Lore: online popular theories claim a hidden structure or pyramid in the Alaska Range near Mt Hayes.

themes.name: Naga
themes.lore: Lore: serpent deities of Hindu and Buddhist tradition, said in Mekong legend to live in the river and guard temples.

themes.name: Hopi ant people
themes.lore: Lore: popular theories retell a Hopi account of 'ant people' who sheltered the Hopi underground, and link it to visitors from the sky. These are outside claims, not Hopi teaching as recorded by the Tribe.

themes.name: Atlantis
themes.lore: Lore: Plato's island that sank in a day and a night; popular theories place it at many real sites.

themes.name: Lemuria
themes.lore: Lore: a lost continent first proposed in 19th-century science and now a popular legend of a sunken Pacific or Indian Ocean civilisation.

themes.name: Mu
themes.lore: Lore: a lost Pacific continent popularised in the 1920s, linked by popular theories to Yonaguni and Nan Madol.

themes.name: Antarctica lost civilisation and pole shift
themes.lore: Lore: popular theories claim Antarctica held a lost civilisation before a sudden physical pole shift moved the crust. Kept apart from the documented fact of geomagnetic reversals (see fact).

fact.text: Earth's magnetic field has reversed polarity many times, recorded in lavas and sediments; reversals have no set period (from about 10,000 to over 50 million years apart), take hundreds to thousands of years, and the last was about 780,000 years ago. This is a magnetic reversal, not a physical shift of the crust or poles.

themes.name: Hidden-realm caves
themes.lore: Lore: caves said in legend to lead to hidden or underworld realms, such as Xibalba, Patala, Hades, Agartha, Telos, the hollow earth and the beyul hidden valleys.

patterns.name: Australian law that travels with you
patterns.question: What Australian (Commonwealth) law and official guidance keeps applying to any Australian traveller while overseas, and what needs handling before leaving and on return?
sources: Commonwealth agencies: Smartraveller and DFAT, Australian Border Force, DAFF biosecurity, ATO, Services Australia, AEC, AFP, Attorney-General's Department, Defence
fields: laws[]: topic, rule, level, source, checked
rules: General information for any Australian traveller, held once on Australia's own record. Not tied to any person or home address.
Unvetted is not permitted. No record is shown as not yet checked, never as no rules.
State each rule from the agency's own page, in plain words, with the source.

patterns.name: Births and family support
patterns.question: How many children are born here and how is that changing, and what do governments offer families: payments at birth, parental leave, childcare, tax relief and other incentives?
sources: UN World Population Prospects (births per woman, births, mothers' average age)
the government department that pays or sets the support
fields: items[]: area, kind (figure or law), changing (true for a dated change), evidence when it differs from the record, text, source, checked
rules: Figures come from the UN or the national statistics office, with their year.
Support is recorded with who pays it, who can get it and its amount in local currency and AUD (with the rate and date).
Most support is for residents or citizens: say who qualifies, and never imply a visitor can claim it.
Describe, don't moralise. No ranking of places or cultures.
Never store anything about the traveller's own family or plans.

patterns.name: Consular reach
patterns.question: Where is the nearest Australian mission or partner able to help, and does it cover this place?
rules: Institutional offices only. No staff names, phone numbers or private contacts.
Skipped for the home country (Australia): an Australian passport holder needs no entry permission there.

patterns.name: Culture and protocol
patterns.question: How does this place ask visitors to arrive and behave, in its own words: names, greetings, welcome and acknowledgement, sacred and restricted places, photography and story permissions, reciprocity, dress, and who holds cultural authority?
sources: the community, nation or local government's own published visitor guidance
cultural authority bodies named by that community
rules: Connective, not assimilative: record each place's own guidance in its own terms; never write cultural rules for a community.
Cultural authority over information stays with the community. Where nothing is published, the status is ask-locally, with who to ask.
Record the place's own names first, then the outside name.
Optional GAJRA Earth thread: the local words for joyful, responsible and abundance, and ideas that do not translate.
Describe, don't lecture. No ranking of cultures and no outsider verdicts.

patterns.name: Culture cycles
patterns.question: Which public holidays, cultural and religious calendars, festivals and community closures shape access and protocol?
rules: Machine holiday data is a signal; community-declared closures come from the community's own channel.
Moving calendars (lunar, Islamic, Hindu and others) are re-dated each year.

patterns.name: Hire a local registered drone pilot, or get footage legally
patterns.question: Is there an official register or search tool of certified drone operators here, what licence or certificate must a commercial operator hold, can a foreign visitor fly commercially or must they hire a local operator, and what legal routes exist to existing aerial footage?
sources: the national aviation authority (for example CASA, CAA, FAA, Transport Canada, MLIT, EASA and national authorities)
state, park or council permit offices
national tourism boards' and film commissions' own media libraries
fields: register: {exists (true, false or null), name, url}
rules: Part of the drone rules: always collected, shown on the site only when Your view's Drone photography toggle is on.
Laws stack: national aviation rules first, then state or province permits, then city, council or park permits. A level with no record is not yet checked.
Official sources only. Never cite a commercial marketplace; mention that such platforms exist only if an official page says so.
register.exists false only when an official page says there is no public list; otherwise null.

patterns.name: Entry permission
patterns.question: Can an Australian passport holder enter, under what status, for how long, and what must be done before arrival?
rules: Primary government sources only for the status. Organiser or airline pages are signals.
Record pre-arrival steps (arrival cards, e-authorisations) separately from the visa status.
Skipped for the home country (Australia): an Australian passport holder needs no entry permission there.

patterns.name: Health entry requirements
patterns.question: Are any vaccinations, certificates or health declarations required to enter?
rules: Entry requirements only. Personal health details are never stored.
Skipped for the home country (Australia): an Australian passport holder needs no entry permission there.

patterns.name: Languages
patterns.question: Which languages are official or national here, how widely is English spoken, and where is English easiest to get by (cities, regions, tourist areas)?
sources: the country's constitution or language law
fields: items[]: area, kind (law or figure), evidence when it differs from the record, text, source, checked
rules: Record the place's own languages first, including Indigenous and sign languages where they're recognised.
English capacity is an estimate with its source and year; a test-taker index is a signal, not a census.
Hotspots are places with a published score or official figure, never impressions.
Describe, don't rank people. No language is treated as better than another.

patterns.name: Local law for visitors
patterns.question: Which laws at this level could a visitor break without knowing: conduct, alcohol, drugs and medicines, photography, filming, dress and public behaviour, speech and religion, relationships, wildlife and biosecurity, camping and fires, driving, currency and goods?
sources: the level's own legislation or by-law register
official visitor guidance from that government
fields: laws[]: topic, rule, penalty_signal, level, source, checked
rules: Laws stack: a visitor is bound by every level at once, so a brief shows national, state and local rules together.
Unvetted is not permitted. A level with no record is shown as not yet checked, never as no rules.
State the rule from the law or the government's own guidance, in plain words, with the source. No moral commentary.
Topics can be added to this list; every place then shows the new topic as not yet checked.

Drone rules (topic drones) are collected like any other topic at every level: national aviation authority, then state or province, then city, council or park. The site shows them only when the Your view drone toggle is on.

patterns.name: Money and cost signal
patterns.question: What currency, cash and card realities and rough daily cost should be expected?
rules: Costs in AUD with the conversion rate and date. A cost signal is never a quote.

patterns.name: Psychoactive substances
patterns.question: What do law and custom here say about alcohol, tobacco and vaping, cannabis, and psychedelic and emerging medicines (MDMA, psilocybin, ayahuasca and others): possession, use, buying, bringing them in, medical, therapeutic and ceremonial access, penalties, and what's changing?
sources: the level's own legislation and health regulator
Smartraveller's drugs, alcohol and local laws sections
the community's own published guidance for ceremonial use
fields: items[]: substance, kind (law, custom, safety or figure), changing (true for a dated change), evidence when it differs from the record, text, source, checked
rules: Record the law as it stands at each level, from country down: states, cities and communities can differ.
Medical, therapeutic and ceremonial access is recorded with who authorises it; a retreat or clinic's own claims are a signal.
Bringing a substance in is recorded separately from using it there, and carrying it home is Australian law.
Describe, don't moralise or advise use. No ranking of places or cultures.
Never store anything about the traveller's own use or prescriptions.

patterns.name: Seasons and visitor flow
patterns.question: How does the year move here: weather seasons, cyclone or monsoon windows, peak, shoulder and quiet visitor months?
rules: Twelve months, each with season, hazard window and visitor flow, so places can be compared month by month.

patterns.name: Visa preparation
patterns.question: What steps, documents and lead time does an Australian passport holder need to prepare before entering, and what is the visa cost signal?
rules: Steps and document lists come from the destination's own pages. Anything carried from Luke's earlier repos is a baseline: status imported or baseline-only, evidence legacy-baseline, needs_recheck true, with the origin repo, commit and claim id in provenance.
Set needs_recheck to false only after every step, document and cost has been reread at an official source; then set status steps-found and redate checked.
Fees are structured once reread: fees: [{item, amount (number, 0 for free), currency (ISO 4217), aud (optional, with rate_date), url, checked}]. cost_aud_baseline stays as the historical signal.
Costs are signals in AUD with the date they were read. Never store passport numbers, bookings or personal documents.
Skipped for the home country (Australia).

patterns.name: Works and purpose fit
patterns.question: How do this place and Luke's works meet: books, music, Aura, founder opportunities?
sources: data/feeds (GAJRA Earth Ahead: AI governance events and open doors)
rules: Runs on places carrying a works tag. Signals, not endorsements.

patterns.name: Year ahead
patterns.question: What dated events in the next twelve months change access, prices or atmosphere: elections, major events, scheduled rule changes?
sources: data/feeds (GAJRA Earth Ahead and others: signals to confirm at source)
fields: events[]: date, what, effect, url, by, category (optional; required when by is official-events and the event is a festival or conference)
rules: A date must come from a source. 'Later this year' is not a date.
Optional event field 'category' must be one of event_categories. Adult (18+) events use dating-marriage-adult and must come from the organiser's own site.

patterns.name: Special permit zones
patterns.question: Beyond national entry, what extra permits, consents, caps, guides, fees or lead times apply to this place or anything inside it?
sources: zone authority (land council, park, regional or island government)
fields: layers[]: type, authority, process, lead_time_days, activities, url, checked
rules: Scan every ancestor and descendant: a national visa never covers a zone permit by itself.
Community consent belongs to the community. Record its published process; never presume an outcome.
Insurance is recorded only where it is a legal, entry, permit or venue requirement.
Each layer's lead time is subtracted from the travel window to give a latest safe start date.
Filming, research and commercial work often need their own permit inside a zone; check each planned activity.
